papers.title: Do They Do as They Are Told? Investigating Coding Agents' Adherence to Explicit Instructions in Context Files
papers.abstract: Developers increasingly rely on agent context files (ACFs), persistent, project-scoped artifacts such as this http URL, to steer the behavior of autonomous coding agents without renegotiating expectations at every interaction. Yet this governance mechanism rests on an untested assumption: that instructions written into an ACF are actually carried out, rather than ignored or loosely followed. Existing studies describe what ACFs contain, but not whether individual instructions are followed, leaving open which guidance can be trusted. We address this gap through an empirical study of real-world ACF snapshots and their linked agent-generated commits: characterizing the explicit, actionable instructions ACFs encode, operationalizing them into executable measurement scripts, and using these scripts to assess instruction-level compliance. We find that most observable instructions can be operationalized and that agents follow ACF guidance more often than not, but adherence splits sharply between instructions followed consistently and those never respected, with differences across instruction categories and coding agents. This split shows where ACF guidance works and where it does not, pointing to instruction types that may need rewriting and to agents that may need enforcement beyond the ACF. These findings lay the groundwork for systematic approaches to specifying, verifying, and enforcing project-specific instructions in autonomous software development.

translation.title: Do They Do as They Are Told? Investigating Coding Agents' Adherence to Explicit Instructions in Context Files
translation.abstract: Developers increasingly rely on agent context files (ACFs), persistent, project-scoped artifacts such as this http URL, to steer the behavior of autonomous coding agents without renegotiating expectations at every interaction. Yet this governance mechanism rests on an untested assumption: that instructions written into an ACF are actually carried out, rather than ignored or loosely followed. Existing studies describe what ACFs contain, but not whether individual instructions are followed, leaving open which guidance can be trusted. We address this gap through an empirical study of real-world ACF snapshots and their linked agent-generated commits: characterizing the explicit, actionable instructions ACFs encode, operationalizing them into executable measurement scripts, and using these scripts to assess instruction-level compliance. We find that most observable instructions can be operationalized and that agents follow ACF guidance more often than not, but adherence splits sharply between instructions followed consistently and those never respected, with differences across instruction categories and coding agents. This split shows where ACF guidance works and where it does not, pointing to instruction types that may need rewriting and to agents that may need enforcement beyond the ACF. These findings lay the groundwork for systematic approaches to specifying, verifying, and enforcing project-specific instructions in autonomous software development.

papers.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
papers.abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestration. AutoManifold conditions every stage of its design on user-specified structural preservation preferences, and iteratively refines the algorithm configuration through an LLM-guided, metric-grounded iterative loop. We compare the generated algorithms against the three strongest and most frequently used SOTA methods (t-SNE, UMAP, and PaCMAP) on real-world datasets spanning different difficulty regimes under identical evaluation infrastructure. The results demonstrate that LLM-driven, priority-conditioned algorithm synthesis can move beyond hyperparameter tuning, producing genuinely new algorithms that outperform traditional hand-designed methods in their ability to steer towards user-specified properties without compromising the intrinsic structure in the original data. The code of AutoManifold is available at this https URL.

papers.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and autonomous agents are creating new opportunities for hardware design optimization. This paper examines three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: (1) Realistic benchmarking. We discuss reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks that evaluate optimization opportunities under realistic EDA workflows. (2) Tool-grounded RTL optimization. We present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, while continuously improving through reusable optimization skills. Evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr.~RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21\%/17\% with a 6\% area reduction over commercial synthesis. (3) Design-specific synthesis optimization. We explore agent-driven synthesis script tuning and the discovery of executable synthesis algorithms across intermediate representations, technology-independent optimization, and technology mapping. Finally, we envision AI-native design automation that jointly explores architectural, RTL, and EDA algorithm design spaces, guided by verification constraints and implementation feedback.

translation.title: 迈向自主RTL与综合优化：基准测试与自我改进智能体
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）与自主智能体的最新进展为硬件设计优化创造了新机遇。本文考察了面向自主RTL与综合优化的三个相互关联的方向：（1）现实基准测试。我们讨论了基于参考和开放式的RTL优化基准，用于在真实EDA工作流下评估优化机会。（2）基于工具的RTL优化。我们提出Dr. RTL，一个多智能体框架，可自动化关键路径分析、RTL重写和实现级评估，并通过可复用的优化技能持续自我改进。在20个真实RTL设计上的评估显示，Dr. RTL相较商业综合平均实现21%/17%的WNS/TNS提升和6%的面积缩减。（3）面向特定设计的综合优化。我们探索了智能体驱动的综合脚本调优，以及在中间表示、工艺无关优化和工艺映射各阶段可执行综合算法的发现。最后，我们展望了AI原生的设计自动化，即在验证约束和实现反馈的引导下，联合探索架构、RTL和EDA算法设计空间。
translation.brief: 针对自主RTL与综合优化缺乏现实基准和自动化工具的问题，提出真实基准体系及通过可复用优化技能持续自我改进的多智能体RTL优化框架。

papers.title: Input-to-State Safety and Small-Gain Theorems for Large-Scale Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies the safety verification problem for a general class of large-scale systems characterized by multiple safety indicator functions. Each safety indicator function satisfies a trajectory-based input-to-state safety (ISSf) estimate that provides a lower bound on its value along system trajectories in terms of the initial state, external inputs, and the other safety indicator functions, whose influence is quantified by continuous and nondecreasing gain functions. Within this framework, we establish a safety-oriented small-gain theorem and its corresponding corollaries that enable compositional and scalable safety verification of the interconnected system, provided that the interconnection gain functions satisfy a small-gain condition on the negative real axis. This condition concerns only the neighborhood of the safety boundary, thereby facilitating the application of our results to safety verification of multi-agent systems under distributed control. Our proof combines small-gain techniques with the lower-bound structure of ISSf estimates and develops an inductive comparison argument that establishes the ISSf property for the overall system throughout the maximal interval of existence. As an application, we establish robust safety for the natural distributed "half-spring" controller, theoretically supporting the computationally efficient and inspiring approach to safety-critical control of multi-agent systems in the presence of obstacles and external disturbances.

translation.title: 大规模非线性系统的输入到状态安全与小增益定理
translation.abstract: 本文研究由多个安全指标函数刻画的一类一般大规模系统的安全验证问题。每个安全指标函数满足基于轨迹的输入到状态安全（ISSf）估计，该估计依据初始状态、外部输入及其他安全指标函数给出其沿系统轨迹取值的下界，其中各函数的影响由连续且非递减的增益函数量化。在此框架下，我们建立了面向安全的小增益定理及其相关推论，只要互联增益函数在负实轴上满足小增益条件，即可实现互联系统的组合式、可扩展安全验证。该条件仅涉及安全边界的邻域，从而便于将结果应用于分布式控制下多智能体系统的安全验证。我们的证明将小增益技术与ISSf估计的下界结构相结合，并发展了归纳比较论证，在整个最大存在区间上建立整体系统的ISSf性质。作为应用，我们为自然分布式"半弹簧"控制器建立了鲁棒安全性，为障碍物与外部扰动下多智能体系统安全关键控制中计算高效且富有启发性的方法提供了理论支撑。
translation.brief: 针对大规模非线性互联系统的可扩展安全验证问题，提出基于ISSf估计和安全导向小增益定理的组合式验证框架。

papers.title: Multi-Objective Scheduling of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows in Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly composed into multi-agent workflows to accomplish complex and multi-step tasks. As the open-weight models continue to close the performance gap with the proprietary ones, model parameters are becoming a less significant source of competitive advantage in the artificial intelligence market. Yet how these models are efficiently scheduled onto distributed infrastructure such as the cloud, with respect to overall latency, monetary cost and resource utilization, remains largely unaddressed in the literature despite being an increasingly critical problem. Existing agentic workflow frameworks mostly focus on output quality and task success rates over popular benchmarks, rarely accounting for execution dynamics of LLM-based agents such as inference latency, computation power of heterogeneous resources, cloud-specific billing period and resource provisioning overheads. Therefore, this paper formulates multi-agent scheduling in cloud computing as a multi-objective optimization problem that jointly minimizes makespan and cost while maximizing resource utilization. Building on this formulation, we propose MO-SAIC (Multi-Objective Scheduling of Multi-Agent Workflows in Cloud Computing), a scheduling framework comprising four multi-objective schedulers with Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), Weighted-Sum Genetic Algorithm (W-GA), a multi-objective adaptation of Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time (MO-HEFT) and a random baseline (RAND). We evaluate the schedulers from the workflow scheduling, multi-objective optimization and system perspectives to measure their overall performance, quality of their Pareto-optimal fronts and impacts of workflow topology, cloud resource composition and scalability parameters. We report the experimental results with their statistical significance via the Wilcoxon test.

translation.title: 云计算中基于LLM的多智能体工作流多目标调度
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）日益被组合成多智能体工作流以完成复杂的多步任务。随着开源权重模型不断缩小与专有模型的性能差距，模型参数正成为AI市场中较次要的竞争优势来源。然而，如何将这些模型高效调度到云端等分布式基础设施上，以兼顾整体时延、成本和资源利用率，尽管日益关键，文献中却鲜有研究。现有智能体工作流框架大多只关注流行基准上的输出质量和任务成功率，很少考虑LLM智能体的执行动态，如推理时延、异构资源算力、云特有的计费周期和资源供给开销。因此，本文将云计算中的多智能体调度形式化为一个多目标优化问题，在最小化工期（makespan）和成本的同时最大化资源利用率。基于该形式化，我们提出MO-SAIC（云计算中多智能体工作流的多目标调度），该调度框架包含四种多目标调度器：基于非支配排序遗传算法II（NSGA-II）、加权和遗传算法（W-GA）、多目标异构最早完成时间算法（MO-HEFT）以及随机基线（RAND）。我们从工作流调度、多目标优化和系统三个角度评估各调度器的整体性能、Pareto最优前沿质量，以及工作流拓扑、云资源组成和可扩展性参数的影响，并通过Wilcoxon检验报告了实验结果的统计显著性。
translation.brief: 针对LLM多智能体工作流在云上调度缺乏多目标优化方法的问题，将其形式化为多目标优化并构建包含NSGA-II等多种调度器的MO-SAIC框架。

papers.title: Exploiting What NVIDIA Profilers Hide: Fast and Accurate Analytical GPU Performance Modeling
papers.abstract: GPUs have become essential to many fields, including AI and scientific computing. As GPUs grow more complex, the design space of their hardware configurations becomes increasingly large, yet cycle-level simulators remain too slow to explore it. Analytical models make this exploration much faster. However, existing GPU analytical models fall short of accurately predicting performance across hardware configurations, because they re-estimate or scale every stall of a warp on the target configuration. We observe that fixed-latency stalls stay the same across configurations, whereas queueing stalls vary with the pressure on each hardware unit. Based on this observation, we propose ForeSight, a queueing analytical model that reuses the fixed-latency stalls measured on GPU hardware and recomputes the queueing stalls of each hardware unit from its pressure. To provide ForeSight with the counter values of each hardware unit, we build UnitSight, a profiler that recovers these values, which NVIDIA's official profilers hide by aggregating across units. Our evaluation on hardware configurations of nine NVIDIA GPUs shows that ForeSight predicts kernel execution time with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 8.3%, compared with 14.1% for the best baseline. ForeSight also predicts the end-to-end execution time of LLM inference on vLLM with a MAPE of 2.0%. It runs 49x faster than the cycle-level simulator Accel-Sim and faster than interval-based models such as GCoM. With the aid of ForeSight, we explore configurations derived from the H20 GPU for LLM inference and find one with 1.78x its performance/cost.

translation.title: 挖掘NVIDIA性能分析器隐藏的信息：快速且准确的分析式GPU性能建模
translation.abstract: GPU已成为AI和科学计算等众多领域的关键工具。随着GPU日益复杂，其硬件配置的设计空间不断扩大，而周期级模拟器仍太慢而无法探索该空间。分析模型使这种探索大大加速。然而，现有GPU分析模型难以在不同硬件配置间准确预测性能，因为它们会对目标配置上warp的每一次停顿进行重新估计或缩放。我们观察到，固定时延停顿在各配置间保持不变，而排队停顿则随各硬件单元上的压力而变化。基于这一观察，我们提出ForeSight，一种排队分析模型，它复用在GPU硬件上测得的固定时延停顿，并根据各硬件单元的压力重新计算其排队停顿。为向ForeSight提供各硬件单元的计数器值，我们构建了UnitSight，一个可恢复这些被NVIDIA官方性能分析器因跨单元聚合而隐藏的值的性能分析器。在九款NVIDIA GPU硬件配置上的评估显示，ForeSight预测kernel执行时间的平均绝对百分比误差（MAPE）为8.3%，而最佳基线为14.1%。ForeSight对vLLM上LLM推理端到端执行时间的预测MAPE为2.0%。其运行速度比周期级模拟器Accel-Sim快49倍，也比GCoM等基于区间的模型更快。借助ForeSight，我们探索了从H20 GPU衍生的LLM推理配置，并找到一个性能/成本比达其1.78倍的配置。
translation.brief: 针对GPU分析模型跨配置预测不准确的问题，提出复用固定时延停顿并按硬件单元压力重算排队停顿的排队分析模型ForeSight，并构建UnitSight分析器恢复被NVIDIA性能分析器聚合隐藏的计数器值。

papers.title: DisasterAgent: An Evidence-Driven Agent for Verifiable Disaster Report Generation From Remote Sensing Imagery
papers.abstract: Remote sensing disaster assessment is moving from simple damage classification toward comprehensive report-level analysis. In this setting, responders need not only damage descriptions but also verifiable evidence to guide response and recovery. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) and tool-augmented agents offer strong multimodal reasoning and perception, but they struggle to provide the evidence required for high-stakes verification. To address these limitations, we propose DisasterAgent, an evidence-driven agent that uses a Perception-Augmentation-Generation workflow to generate verifiable disaster reports from bitemporal optical imagery. DisasterAgent first invokes a specialized vision expert toolkit in the perception phase to build a Spatiotemporal Perception Graph (STPG), serving as a structured memory to store and organize disaster-induced changes across space and time. Evidence-based Augmentation (EA) then extracts evidence from the STPG, attaching inline citations that form a closed evidence loop from each statement to the supporting visual evidence. Extensive experiments on the DisasterM3 and RSCC benchmarks demonstrate that DisasterAgent consistently outperforms general-domain VLMs, remote sensing-specialized models, and existing remote sensing agents. Notably, compared with the original model, it improves the average score for disaster report generation on DisasterM3 by 13.5\% and ST5-SCS on RSCC by 15.34\%, providing a more accurate and verifiable solution for disaster emergency response. The code will be available at this https URL.

translation.title: DisasterAgent：一种基于证据驱动的智能体，用于从遥感影像生成可验证的灾害报告
translation.abstract: 遥感灾害评估正从简单的损毁分类走向综合的报告级分析。在这一场景中，响应人员不仅需要损毁描述，还需要可验证的证据来指导响应与恢复。近期的视觉-语言模型（VLM）和工具增强智能体提供了强大的多模态推理与感知能力，但难以提供高风险验证所需的证据。为解决这些局限，我们提出DisasterAgent，一个证据驱动的智能体，采用感知-增强-生成工作流，从双时相光学影像生成可验证的灾害报告。DisasterAgent首先在感知阶段调用专门的视觉专家工具包，构建时空感知图（STPG），作为结构化记忆来存储和组织灾害引发的时空变化。随后，基于证据的增强（EA）从STPG中提取证据，并附加内联引用，形成从每条陈述到支持性视觉证据的闭环证据链。在DisasterM3和RSCC基准上的大量实验表明，DisasterAgent持续优于通用领域VLM、遥感专用模型和现有遥感智能体。值得注意的是，与原始模型相比，它将DisasterM3上灾害报告生成的平均分提升了13.5%，将RSCC上的ST5-SCS提升了15.34%，为灾害应急响应提供了更准确、可验证的解决方案。代码将在此https URL提供。
translation.brief: 针对遥感灾害报告生成缺乏可验证证据的问题，提出证据驱动的DisasterAgent，通过时空感知图与内联引用构建证据闭环以生成可验证报告。

papers.title: LLM Validation Makes Minimal-Pair Benchmarks Easier for Language Models
papers.abstract: Minimal-pair benchmarks are only as good as their labels, and LLMs are an obvious substitute for costly human validation. We test it on BLiMP (English) and QFrBLiMP (Quebec French), the two public minimal-pair datasets releasing every forced-choice human judgment. Three LLMs validate by forced choice, by rating, and as a panel, scored against human panels of one, three and five judges in two pre-registered phases. On BLiMP, forced-choice validators agree with held-out human majorities more often than five-judge panels, yet catch far fewer pairs whose label humans reject than one judge does. By point estimate, no validator is worth more than one judge. The errors are not random. On both datasets, across 10 open LMs, human-supported pairs that the pre-registered LLM filter flags are 18.9 points harder than those it accepts, in all 70 LM-validator combinations, and harder than pairs a single human judge flags. Filtering thus removes items on which LMs fail but humans do not, raising accuracy more than random removal. A protocol frozen before any output replicates the gap and the lift on Dutch BLiMP-NL. LLM validation makes minimal-pair benchmarks easier for the models they are meant to test; we release code, validator outputs and item-level scores.

papers.title: Auditing LLM Pseudo-Label Distillation for Review Informativeness at E-Commerce Scale
papers.abstract: We study hard-label distillation from Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite to compact encoders on 5.34 million Turkish marketplace reviews. A strict new-SKU temporal test measures teacher fidelity; a separate, teacher-label-blind audit by one company annotator measures editorial agreement. An H3 category prefix slightly improves teacher fidelity on the full new-SKU test. On the 16,000-review chronological audit subset, it instead reduces agreement with both Gemini and the annotator, with a clearer paired difference for CORN than for cross entropy. Thus the context effect depends on the evaluation population, and teacher fidelity alone does not establish editorial alignment. Under the measured offline configurations, a single-L4 student pipeline processes reviews 50.2 times faster than the teacher pipeline.

papers.title: Scaling Shapley Energy Attribution to Large LLM Batches
papers.abstract: LLM services have become essential infrastructure for applications such as chat assistants and coding agents. Service providers need to attribute resource consumption to individual requests for purposes such as billing. Among these resources, energy is a key metric for assessing the cost of serving each request. However, serving engines batch requests together, and GPUs report only aggregate energy consumption. Providers typically estimate each request's share in proportion to its token consumption, but this approach can produce substantially unfair estimates. The Shapley value provides a principled solution to fair energy allocation, but computing it directly requires $2^N-1$ GPU runs for $N$ requests, which is infeasible for large batches. To address this problem, we propose StepSplit. Across GPU generations, we observe that the energy consumed by each inference step, a forward pass over a batch, consists of a shared energy, largely due to reading model weights, and a request-specific energy. We derive a closed-form Shapley value: each request is charged its own energy plus an equal part of the shared energy of every step in which it participates. A microbenchmark of 2.5-17.8 minutes calibrates both parts of the step energy once per model and GPU configuration. Under static batching, StepSplit uses this closed form in a single pass over the scheduler log. Under continuous batching, removing a request can change how the remaining requests are batched, so StepSplit adds a correction to the closed form, computed by replaying the scheduler on a CPU. We evaluate StepSplit against Shapley values measured using 529,513 GPU runs. Under static batching with batch sizes of 8-256, StepSplit achieves an $L_1$ error of 0.4-4.3%, compared with 13.4-61.3% for token-proportional allocation. Under continuous batching with 8-128 requests, the corresponding errors are 0.5-6.4% and 20.6-71.7%.

papers.title: WAM is capable in BEHAVIOR-1K: the 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
papers.abstract: This work presents the 2nd-place solution (Team IF1001) to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, which evaluates mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks. Our method is built on a powerful world action model (WAM), Cosmos 3. We improve Cosmos 3 by using richer visual history, task-progress conditioning, and task-group and skill-specific LoRA adapters. During inference, we apply a separate progress estimator to supply task-progress context, and use task- and progress-conditioned routing to select a task-group or skill-specific policy, complemented by action-candidate aggregation, rolling inpainting, and task-specific temporal and gripper control. To meet the minimum inference requirement of 1 FPS, we use neither recursive self-improvement (RSI) nor agentic harness methods and rely on no closed-source models; during official private-test evaluation, our system handled concurrent requests across 100 evaluation ports with limited hardware resources, sustaining an average end-to-end inference rate above 2 FPS per port. Our method achieves a mean Q-score of 0.613 and a full-task success rate of 40.9%, averaged over 3 self-evaluation rounds across all 100 tasks. On the official private test set, with 20 instances per task, our system achieves a mean Q-score of 0.615 and a full-task success rate of 41.2%.

papers.title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
papers.abstract: Typed-decision encoders answer a question about a text in one forward pass, but their behaviour outside English is rarely measured on a fixed yardstick. We release PolyRoute: 322 native-language support messages in 12 languages and 9 writing systems, 156 code-mixed or romanised messages (Hinglish, Spanglish, Arabizi), 967 optional native training rows, and a protocol for a three-way department-routing decision. Labels come from Qwen3.8-27B with a blind second pass (91% of candidates kept); an independent model, gemma4-31b, agrees on 97.2% of test items, and the largest character 5-gram similarity between any test text and any training text is 0.33. A leaderboard of 13 systems gives 61.2% for the English-root checkpoint, 77.3% for the shipped multilingual one and 96.6% for the best fine-tune; TF-IDF with logistic regression reaches 91.9%. On four withheld languages the three multilingual systems score 77%, 90% and 93%. On code-mixed text the English root (85%) is nominally ahead of the shipped multilingual checkpoint (79%; p=0.134). The split resolves differences only above about 4 points. All texts and labels are LLM-generated.

papers.title: Beyond Passive Imitation: On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation for Language Models
papers.abstract: Continual pre-training (CPT) adapts large language models (LLMs) to specialized domains, yet its standard next-token prediction (NTP) objective treats every corpus token as a fixed target, regardless of its utility to the current model. In a controlled study on the same 1B-token mathematical corpus, we observe sharply different outcomes across base models: NTP improves Llama-3.2-3B's performance on mathematical benchmarks but substantially degrades Qwen3-1.7B-Base's performance, indicating that, under a fixed training recipe, the same training sequences can have model-dependent effects. To address this problem, we introduce On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation (OPMD), which reformulates mid-training from offline text imitation into active, query-driven knowledge acquisition. At selected anchor positions, OPMD samples trajectories from the evolving student policy and applies dense token-level reverse-KL rewards from a frozen teacher, training the model on states it actually visits rather than only on ground-truth prefixes. This on-policy objective reduces the training-generation mismatch of teacher-forced NTP. On MATH-500 and Minerva, OPMD improves the Qwen student over its base performance and outperforms the evaluated NTP baseline, which degrades on both benchmarks. OPMD integrates into CPT pipelines without added inference-time overhead and offers a model-aware alternative to passive domain adaptation.

translation.title: 超越被动模仿：面向语言模型的在线策略中期训练蒸馏
translation.abstract: 持续预训练（CPT）可将大语言模型（LLM）适配到专门领域，但其标准的下一词预测（NTP）目标将语料库中的每个词元都视为固定目标，而不考虑其对当前模型的效用。在一项基于同一个10亿词元数学语料库的受控研究中，我们观察到不同基座模型的结果截然不同：NTP 提升了 Llama-3.2-3B 在数学基准上的表现，却显著降低了 Qwen3-1.7B-Base 的性能，这表明在固定训练配方下，相同的训练序列可能产生依赖于模型的效果。为解决这一问题，我们提出了在线策略中期训练蒸馏（OPMD），将中期训练从离线文本模仿重新表述为主动的、由查询驱动的知识获取。在选定的锚定位置，OPMD 从不断演进的学生策略中采样轨迹，并应用来自冻结教师模型的稠密词元级 reverse-KL 奖励，使模型在其实际访问的状态上训练，而不只是在真实前缀上训练。这一在线策略目标降低了教师强制 NTP 的训练-生成失配。在 MATH-500 和 Minerva 上，OPMD 使 Qwen 学生模型超越了其基座性能，并优于被评估的 NTP 基线（后者在两个基准上均出现退化）。OPMD 可无缝集成到 CPT 流水线中且不增加推理时开销，为被动式领域自适应提供了一种模型感知的替代方案。
translation.brief: 针对 NTP 持续预训练在不同模型上效果不一的问题，提出 OPMD，通过从学生策略采样轨迹并用冻结教师的词元级 reverse-KL 奖励实现在线策略中期训练蒸馏。

papers.title: Uncovering the Memory Hierarchy of Modern NVIDIA GPUs for Accurate Simulation
papers.abstract: Emerging artificial intelligence workloads, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), place unprecedented demands on GPU memory systems. Consequently, architectural innovations increasingly target the memory system to alleviate these bottlenecks. However, existing works still rely on outdated memory hierarchy models that fail to capture the complexities of modern hardware. This fidelity gap leads to inaccurate characterization and could misguide optimization strategies. To bridge this gap, we present GemAtlas, the first systematic reverse engineering of the memory hierarchy in modern NVIDIA GPUs. By developing fine-grained SASS-level benchmarking, we expose critical, previously undocumented micro-architectural details across different cache levels, including cache set associativity, slice-routing and set-indexing hash functions, replacement policies, coherence behavior, and interconnect topologies. We integrate these discovered micro-architecture details into the state-of-the-art GPU simulation framework. The final results demonstrate that GemAtlas reduces the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 31.69% to 22.24% on average across four GPUs. Specifically, GemAtlas reduces the MAPE from 34.04% to 23.98% for real-world LLM operators.

translation.title: 揭示现代 NVIDIA GPU 的内存层次结构以实现精确仿真
translation.abstract: 新兴的人工智能工作负载，尤其是大语言模型（LLM），对 GPU 内存系统提出了前所未有的需求。因此，架构创新日益聚焦于内存系统以缓解这些瓶颈。然而，现有工作仍依赖过时的内存层次模型，无法刻画现代硬件的复杂性。这种保真度差距导致刻画不准确，并可能误导优化策略。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了 GemAtlas，这是首个对现代 NVIDIA GPU 内存层次结构的系统性逆向工程。通过开发细粒度的 SASS 级基准测试，我们揭示了跨各级缓存的此前未被记录的关键微架构细节，包括缓存组相联度、slice 路由与组索引哈希函数、替换策略、一致性行为以及互连拓扑。我们将这些发现的微架构细节集成到最先进的 GPU 仿真框架中。最终结果表明，GemAtlas 将四款 GPU 上的平均绝对百分比误差（MAPE）从 31.69% 降至平均 22.24%。具体而言，对于真实世界的 LLM 算子，GemAtlas 将 MAPE 从 34.04% 降至 23.98%。
translation.brief: 针对 GPU 仿真器内存层次模型过时导致精度不足的问题，通过对现代 NVIDIA GPU 的 SASS 级逆向工程刻画缓存微架构细节并集成到仿真框架中。

papers.title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
papers.abstract: Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

translation.title: 从反事实编辑到人类叙事：基于 LLM 的推荐系统解释生成
translation.abstract: 推荐系统日益影响用户在网络上的发现与消费，但其输出背后的决策逻辑往往不透明。反事实解释（CFX）方法提供了一种有效方式，展示对用户交互历史的哪些改动会改变推荐结果。然而在推荐场景中，CFX 通常需要大量编辑，产生冗长且底层的列表，用户难以理解。此外，大多数评估强调编辑数量，而在很大程度上忽略了生成的 CFX 是否对用户连贯且可操作。我们认为，生成有效 CFX 与传达模型行为之间的这一差距，源于缺乏以用户为中心的抽象以及定性评估的不足。为弥合这一差距，我们研究将大语言模型作为中介，把原始的 CFX 交互编辑列表总结为描述更高层偏好模式的简洁自然语言解释。我们通过偏好优化对这些中介模型在正确性、信息量和语言质量上进行优化，并使用从独立的人工标注数据集导出的经人工校准的指标来评估生成的解释。在 MovieLens-1M 数据集上，跨多个反事实生成器和语言模型，生成的总结整体语言质量较高，而最强的语义结果来自高成功率的 CFX 方法（如 ACCENT 和 SPINRec）。Direct Preference Optimization 在几乎所有评估设置中都提升了语义指标。
translation.brief: 针对反事实解释编辑列表冗长难懂、评估缺乏用户视角的问题，用经偏好优化的 LLM 将其总结为面向用户的自然语言解释。

papers.title: Online Adaptive Clustering in Robust Distributed Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic clustering framework for tube-based model predictive control (MPC) of coupled multi-agent systems. Agents within a cluster coordinate their dynamics explicitly, while couplings from agents outside the cluster are treated as bounded disturbances. For each admissible cluster, we construct a state-dependent mismatch measure from a robust upper bound on its predicted closed-loop cost and an optimistic, partition-independent lower bound. Combining this mismatch with a communication penalty enables online selection of the clustering topology, ranging from centralized to fully decentralized operation. The resulting switching controller is shown to preserve recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction, and to render the closed-loop system practically asymptotically stable. Furthermore, the mismatch provides an upper bound on the finite-horizon performance difference with respect to centralized MPC. An eight-agent spring--damper example illustrates how the controller adapts cooperation while maintaining performance close to centralized MPC with reduced communication.

translation.title: 鲁棒分布式模型预测控制中的在线自适应聚类
translation.abstract: 本文提出了一种面向耦合多智能体系统 tube-based 模型预测控制（MPC）的动态聚类框架。同一聚类内的智能体显式协调其动力学，而来自聚类外智能体的耦合则被视为有界扰动。对于每个可行的聚类，我们基于其预测闭环代价的鲁棒上界和一个乐观的、与划分无关的下界，构建了一个状态相关的失配度量。将该失配度量与通信惩罚相结合，可在线选择聚类拓扑，范围涵盖从集中式到完全分散式运行。所得到的切换控制器被证明可保持递归可行性与约束满足，并使闭环系统具有实际渐近稳定性。此外，该失配度量给出了与集中式 MPC 相比的有限时域性能差异的上界。一个八智能体弹簧-阻尼器示例说明了控制器如何在保持接近集中式 MPC 性能的同时减少通信、自适应地调整协作。
translation.brief: 针对耦合多智能体系统的分布式 MPC 聚类拓扑难以选择的问题，提出基于闭环代价上下界失配度量的在线自适应聚类框架，兼顾递归可行性与稳定性。

papers.title: OpenRE-Bench: A Benchmark Harness for Multi-Agent Requirements Engineering with Mined GitHub Issues
papers.abstract: OpenRE-Bench is an open-source benchmarking infrastructure for large language model (LLM) based multi-agent requirements-engineering (RE) frameworks. Such frameworks are increasingly common, but they use different agent roles, negotiation policies, and output shapes, and are typically evaluated on their own runtimes, metrics, and small sets of curated system descriptions, which makes fair, reproducible comparison difficult. OpenRE-Bench addresses this with four reusable pieces: a shared run harness with one input, phase-artifact, and metric contract; an adapter mechanism through which a framework joins by implementing a single adapter, leaving cases, metrics, and other adapters untouched; a reproducible GitHub issue-mining pipeline that grows the corpus from real feature requests; and a versioned case suite. As a demonstration, we mine 3,000 fetched issues across five projects (three languages, five domains) into five cases, package them with five hand-built cases as the compact v1.0 suite, and run three heterogeneous frameworks (MARE and iReDev as paper-faithful reimplementations, plus QUARE) under one protocol. OpenRE-Bench originated as the evaluation back-end of our QUARE study and has since been reused by two further studies of our group. It is released with a pinned environment, a Docker image, frozen API snapshots, a 651-test suite, and the full pool of 1,396 filtered issues behind the mined cases.

translation.title: OpenRE-Bench：基于挖掘的 GitHub Issue 的多智能体需求工程基准测试框架
translation.abstract: OpenRE-Bench 是一个面向基于大语言模型（LLM）的多智能体需求工程（RE）框架的开源基准测试基础设施。此类框架日益普遍，但它们使用不同的智能体角色、协商策略和输出形式，并且通常在各自的运行时、指标和少量人工整理的系统描述上进行评估，这使得公平、可复现的比较十分困难。OpenRE-Bench 通过四个可复用的组件解决这一问题：一个具有统一输入、阶段产物和指标契约的共享运行框架（run harness）；一种适配器机制，框架只需实现单个适配器即可接入，而无需改动用例、指标和其他适配器；一条可复现的 GitHub issue 挖掘流水线，用于从真实功能请求中扩充语料；以及一个带版本的用例套件。作为演示，我们将五个项目（三种语言、五个领域）中抓取的 3,000 条 issue 挖掘为五个用例，与五个手工构建的用例一起打包为紧凑的 v1.0 套件，并在统一协议下运行三个异构框架（MARE 和 iReDev 作为忠实于论文的重实现，以及 QUARE）。OpenRE-Bench 最初作为我们 QUARE 研究的评估后端，此后已被我们团队的另外两项研究复用。它以固定环境、Docker 镜像、冻结的 API 快照、包含 651 项测试的测试套件以及挖掘用例背后的全部 1,396 条过滤 issue 的完整池的形式发布。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 多智能体需求工程框架难以公平、可复现比较的问题，构建包含统一运行契约、适配器机制和真实 GitHub issue 挖掘流水线的开源基准 OpenRE-Bench。

papers.title: Safety and Connectivity Certificates for Finite-Time Formation Transitions
papers.abstract: Finite-time formation transitions are useful for coordinating multi-agent systems in time-critical missions, but convergence to a prescribed formation in finite time does not guarantee collision avoidance or communication connectivity during the transition. Existing approaches address finite-time coordination and safety-constrained formation control, yet explicit connections between disagreement during transitions, formation geometry, and coupling-gain selection need to be developed for certifying safe maneuvers. This paper develops a disagreement-based framework for certifying transient safety and connectivity during finite-time tracking of arbitrary prescribed formation trajectories. Local feedback guarantees exact finite-time tracking with a graph-independent settling-time bound, while a graph-dependent disagreement bound is used to derive sufficient geometric conditions for collision avoidance and connectivity preservation. These conditions further yield an offline coupling-gain selection rule based on the available geometric clearance. Numerical simulations illustrate the trade-off between convergence rate and control effort as the coupling gain increases. They also demonstrate the effectiveness and conservatism of the proposed certificates.

papers.title: TAPCO-G: LLM-Guided Design-Adaptive Timing and Power Co-Optimization with Graph-Based Physical Priors
papers.abstract: Post-placement timing and power co-optimization is critical to meeting setup timing targets and reducing power within placement constraints. A cell replacement can improve timing along one path while increasing power or reducing slack on others. Conventional optimizers follow fixed rules for scheduling and accepting repairs, limiting their ability to address design-specific bottlenecks. A large language model (LLM) can propose changes to these rules, but on its own it cannot reliably estimate how a cell replacement affects endpoint slack and power. TAPCO-G combines LLM-guided optimizer adaptation with graph-based physical priors to evaluate candidate cell replacements. The outer loop tunes tool settings using physical-design feedback and revises executable repair policies when tuning stalls. The inner loop anchors delay estimates to static timing analysis snapshots, accounts for upstream driver-load changes, and propagates delay shifts to timing endpoints. It combines these estimates with coarse-to-fine power screening to prioritize candidates for physical trials. TAPCO-G produced placement-legal, logic-equivalent implementations and outscored CERBERUS on all eight ASAP7 benchmarks from the MLCAD 2026 Contest, with a mean quality score gain of 5.516 points, and scored 21.648 points higher than TAPCO on average. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed co-optimization framework.

papers.title: Chem World: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Physics-Aware Framework for Trustworthy Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction is fundamental to computational chemistry and drug formulation research, yet existing benchmarks remain fragmented across datasets, properties, and evaluation protocols, limiting systematic evaluation of model generalization. We introduce Chem World, a large-scale benchmark integrating 17 public datasets with over 800,000 molecular and chemical-system instances across 10 property tracks, covering single-molecule and multi-component systems, including drug solubility. Chem World provides a unified testbed for evaluating molecular representations and compositional modeling across diverse chemical properties. Building on the benchmark, we propose PACM (Physics-Aware Compositional Modeling), which combines molecular representations with composition-aware modeling and domain-specific physical constraints. Extensive experiments show that molecular language models provide strong and transferable representations, while PACM consistently improves prediction across diverse chemical systems. Chem World and our PACM-powered drug-property prediction Agent support generalizable chemical modeling and offer a foundation for AI-assisted biomedical research and drug formulation development.

papers.title: TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data
papers.abstract: Practical Web applications increasingly require agents to interpret long conversations or documents. For inputs exceeding the context windows of large language models (LLMs), memory agents process segments sequentially and retain past information in bounded memory. However, they typically divide inputs into flat token segments without preserving structure or hierarchy, causing three limitations for structured data such as API responses or HTML documents. First, fixed-length segmentation can split fields of the same record, breaking their relationships. Second, segments lack hierarchical information, obscuring their structural context and positions. Third, successive memory updates may discard details of earlier sibling records needed for reasoning on later segments. To address these limitations, we propose TreeAgent, a structure-aware agent that uses the input hierarchy to guide both segment-wise context processing and access to past information. Specifically, TreeAgent constructs segments from complete subtrees and groups of adjacent sibling subtrees to preserve local structural relationships. We provide theoretical guarantees on segment counts to guide token budget selection toward matching the segment count of fixed-length segmentation. We further attach structural paths to the segments for the agent to identify their ancestors and hierarchical positions. We also introduce residual memory links from the segments of low-level children to the segments of high-level parents, enabling direct information flows beyond successive memory updates. We evaluate TreeAgent with four representative memory agents on eight retrieval and aggregation tasks. The inputs are derived from real-world application data in JSON, HTML, YAML, and JavaScript and range from 8K to 1M tokens. TreeAgent improves the average score across the four datasets for all four agents, with 3.61% performance gain on average.

translation.title: TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data
translation.abstract: Practical Web applications increasingly require agents to interpret long conversations or documents. For inputs exceeding the context windows of large language models (LLMs), memory agents process segments sequentially and retain past information in bounded memory. However, they typically divide inputs into flat token segments without preserving structure or hierarchy, causing three limitations for structured data such as API responses or HTML documents. First, fixed-length segmentation can split fields of the same record, breaking their relationships. Second, segments lack hierarchical information, obscuring their structural context and positions. Third, successive memory updates may discard details of earlier sibling records needed for reasoning on later segments. To address these limitations, we propose TreeAgent, a structure-aware agent that uses the input hierarchy to guide both segment-wise context processing and access to past information. Specifically, TreeAgent constructs segments from complete subtrees and groups of adjacent sibling subtrees to preserve local structural relationships. We provide theoretical guarantees on segment counts to guide token budget selection toward matching the segment count of fixed-length segmentation. We further attach structural paths to the segments for the agent to identify their ancestors and hierarchical positions. We also introduce residual memory links from the segments of low-level children to the segments of high-level parents, enabling direct information flows beyond successive memory updates. We evaluate TreeAgent with four representative memory agents on eight retrieval and aggregation tasks. The inputs are derived from real-world application data in JSON, HTML, YAML, and JavaScript and range from 8K to 1M tokens. TreeAgent improves the average score across the four datasets for all four agents, with 3.61% performance gain on average.

papers.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
papers.abstract: AI coding harnesses couple language models to shells, filesystems, and network sockets, turning the harness into an automated Living-off-the-Land (LotL) platform: once an adversary injects instructions into retrieved content, dual-use binaries such as bash, curl, and find become the payload. We argue that security in agentic systems is a structural property of the cognitive architecture and permission composition rather than an emergent property of individual models. Static regex blacklists miss structural evasions, whereas LLM-as-a-Judge guardrails incur high latency while over-blocking benign work. We present ActiveSecHarness, a neurosymbolic reference-monitor architecture built around Separation of Intelligence and Authority. It combines (1) Macaroon-inspired HMAC capability tokens across four Trust and Authority Rings, (2) a 2D product taint lattice $\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{trust}} \times \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{sens}}$ and a workspace provenance ledger that prevents secret laundering across disk, (3) deterministic Ring-0 OS/tool guards, and (4) bytecode certificates, split-horizon audit logs, self-healing security test synthesis, and an adaptive UserWikiManager. Across $N=252$ fixtures ($120$ attack, $120$ benign, $12$ kill chains), a live local LLM judge (qwen3:4b) refuses $98.3\%$ of benign work at $142.3\,\mathrm{ms}$ latency, whereas Ring 0 achieves $\mathrm{ABR}=1.000$ and $\mathrm{FPR}=0.000$ in $12.7\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ ($11{,}200\times$ faster). In a multi-step trajectory ablation, an oracle Conseca-style stateless policy misses $4/12$ kill chains ($\mathrm{ABR}=0.667$) and coarse Boolean taint blocks $83.3\%$ of benign workflows, while our 2D product lattice achieves $\mathrm{ABR}=1.000$ and $\mathrm{FPR}=0.000$ at $\approx 20\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ per step.

papers.title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
papers.abstract: Taxonomies are structured knowledge representations that support semantic search, recommendation, product catalog organization, and retrieval-augmented generation. Their automated construction from a fixed set of candidate entities requires more than plausible text generation: the resulting hierarchy must be complete, structurally valid, and semantically coherent. Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising for this task, but iterative free-form generation remains vulnerable to omitted or hallucinated entities, invalid hierarchical relations, and inconsistent organizational principles. We introduce TIGA (Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded Agents), a knowledge-engineering architecture that formulates taxonomy induction as an iterative decision process over an explicit state and constrained action space. TIGA combines executable taxonomy-editing tools, an memory that records tool calls, rationales, and outcomes, and a runtime-adaptive organizational policy that the agent revises during inference. An optional global reviewer evaluates the constructed taxonomy against the candidate set and the active policy. We evaluate TIGA on four benchmark taxonomies using two LLM backbones and compare it with single-shot and iterative prompting-based baselines. TIGA achieves the strongest structural-quality results in most evaluated configurations, but does not dominate on every precision measure. The gains are accompanied by substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time. Ablation results show consistent benefits from the policy and interaction-memory components, whereas the effect of global review depends on the dataset and the available revision budget. These findings characterize tool grounding and runtime policy adaptation as promising but costly mechanisms for improving the controlled construction of structured knowledge representations.

papers.title: Data Quality Challenges in Multimodal Tourism Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Modern recommender systems increasingly consider diverse data modalities to enhance model performance. However, the quality of the underlying multimodal data (e.g. data from social media platforms) has received limited attention so far. Focusing on tourism recommendation, we examine real-world challenges encountered when using datasets from Yelp and Instagram. Issues include noise from fake reviews, hallucinated content from LLMs, modality contradictions, and demographic bias. We outline future directions such as quality-aware fusion, structured and controlled LLM-based content generation to reduce hallucinations, and user group differentiation to improve the robustness and reliability of multimodal recommendation systems.

papers.title: BioXArena-Pro: a research-grade benchmark for autonomous biomedical machine learning agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous builders of biomedical models, but existing benchmarks are small, near saturation or open to leaked information. We present BioXArena-Pro, 64 research-level modelling tasks from eight biomedical domains, each rebuilt from a published study; most hold out whole biological units such as species or cohorts. Across 22 agent configurations, the best scores 55.1 of 100, and the scaffold matters almost as much as the model. We re-ran a published method for every task: where the published recipe applies unchanged, the best agent and the methods tie; on rebuilt tasks the methods trail by 8.2 points, suggesting that agents gain by adapting to new data. Pretrained models (including biological foundation models) matter where the strongest agent uses them: forbidding them decreases its score on those tasks by 9 points. Every task was audited in several AI-assisted rounds and a final human review.

papers.title: LUMIR: Decoupled Multimodal Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Data for Next-POI Recommendation
papers.abstract: As multimodal tourism-related information collected from heterogeneous data sources has become increasingly available, learning effective representations has attracted attention for improving recommendation performance. Existing approaches often tightly couple multimodal fusion with the architecture and optimization objective of a specific downstream model, which limits the generality and reusability of the learned representations. To address these limitations, we propose LUMIR, a decoupled multimodal representation learning framework based on contrastive learning. Multimodal information collected from heterogeneous data sources is first semantically unified into a shared textual representation space using large language models (LLMs). An interaction-aware fusion mechanism is then designed to model cross-modal interactions, while sequential signals are incorporated as a structural constraint to guide representation learning. To evaluate the learned representations, experiments are conducted on a multimodal point-of-interest (POI) dataset under the next-POI recommendation setting across multiple sequential recommendation backbones. The results show that LUMIR consistently outperforms existing multimodal fusion baselines in both accuracy-oriented and beyond-accuracy metrics, demonstrating that decoupling representation learning from downstream optimization provides an effective paradigm for learning reusable multimodal representations. The code is publicly available at this https URL.

papers.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Language-model agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks whose interaction histories exceed the model's active context. They must therefore decide what to write down and what to read back, and when to do either. Recent work has begun to use on-policy distillation (OPD) to make memory control part of the policy, relying on memory tools and compaction protocols that lie outside either model's pre-training. However, this weakens the distillation on both sides: the teacher cannot give useful guidance on an interface it has never used, and the student samples too few meaningful memory actions for that guidance to take effect. To study this problem, we introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym II (CAMG-II), a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shop, Coding, AutoResearch, General, and Visual. Alongside each environment's native task interface, CAMG-II provides ordinary Bash access and an episode-persistent workspace, enabling the policy to create, revise, search, and reuse files as memory across context replacements. We also introduce Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II (CAMP-II), which trains a single policy jointly across all five environments with fully asynchronous OPD to learn this file-based memory behavior directly from a frozen teacher with a prior for file operations. On CAMG-II, CAMP-II obtains 2.97 times the gain of the strongest OPD baseline. The memory behavior CAMP-II learns generalizes to two external benchmarks, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Pro V2, with improved success rates.

papers.title: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment
papers.abstract: Long-horizon personalized agents maintain an evolving memory by continuously deciding what to add, modify, or discard. However, learning an optimal update policy remains challenging. Conventional training relies solely on terminal question-answering accuracy, yielding a coarse feedback signal that treats all intermediate updates identically. Furthermore, update utility is inherently user-specific, as identical memory actions may yield opposite effects across different user personas. Existing methods fail to address this heterogeneity, relying on globally shared evaluation standards with at most a single scalar intermediate reward. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Personalized Memory Rubrics} (\textbf{PMR}), a framework that translates terminal feedback into fine-grained, per-step, and per-user credit assignment. PMR decomposes evaluation into a universal layer capturing cross-persona failure patterns and a per-user adaptive layer modeling individual traits as a specialized delta over the universal baseline. Through \textbf{Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment}, PMR redistributes credit at the token level, selectively amplifying validated decisions on successful trajectories while falling back to standard policy optimization on failed ones to avoid unreliable attribution. The rubric and memory policy \textbf{co-evolve} in a closed loop with anti-circularity guarantees. Crucially, PMR incurs zero inference overhead, operating without any rubric or external judge during deployment. Extensive experiments across four benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains over strong memory-augmented baselines.

translation.title: 个性化记忆准则：通过准则引导的信用分配学习每个用户应记住什么
translation.abstract: 长周期个性化智能体通过持续决定添加、修改或丢弃什么来维护不断演化的记忆，但学习最优更新策略仍具挑战性。传统训练仅依赖终端问答准确率，反馈信号粗糙，对所有中间更新一视同仁；且更新效用天然具有用户特异性，相同的记忆操作在不同用户画像上可能产生相反效果。现有方法未能解决这种异质性，依赖全局共享的评估标准和至多一个标量中间奖励。为此，我们提出个性化记忆准则（PMR）框架，将终端反馈转化为细粒度、按步骤、按用户的信用分配。PMR 将评估分解为捕捉跨画像失败模式的通用层，以及将个体特质建模为通用基线之上专门增量的每用户自适应层。通过准则引导的信用分配，PMR 在 token 级别重新分配信用，选择性地放大成功轨迹上经过验证的决策，而在失败轨迹上回退到标准策略优化以避免不可靠的归因。准则与记忆策略在带有反循环保证的闭环中共同演化。关键在于，PMR 不产生任何推理开销，部署时无需任何准则或外部评判器。在四个基准上的大量实验表明，其相比强记忆增强基线取得一致增益。
translation.brief: 解决个性化智能体记忆更新策略训练中反馈粗糙且忽略用户差异的问题，核心方法是通过将终端反馈分解为通用层与每用户自适应层的准则，实现按步骤、按用户的细粒度信用分配。

papers.title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
papers.abstract: Agent skills have emerged as an effective means of enabling LLM agents to solve complex, interactive tasks by encoding reusable knowledge without modifying model parameters. Recent approaches further improve skill adaptation by distilling reusable experience from agent execution trajectories and evolving skills based on downstream task feedback. However, existing methods primarily represent skills as natural language documents, intertwining procedural logic with descriptive knowledge and making skills difficult to maintain and evolve. To address this limitation, we propose PASE (Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution), a program-aided framework that iteratively evolves skills by associating them with executable programs. Unlike prior approaches that encode trajectory-derived experience primarily in natural language, PASE separates reusable procedural logic into editable programs, enabling targeted updates to executable components while reducing the need to repeatedly revise natural language skills. Extensive experiments across diverse models and benchmarks demonstrate that PASE consistently outperforms all baselines, by achieving over 2.8% improvements. Further analyses show that PASE exhibits greater evolutionary stability and generalisation capability, highlighting the critical role of programmatic knowledge in skill evolution. We will release all data and code via GitHub.

translation.title: 程序辅助的可修补技能演化
translation.abstract: 智能体技能已成为使 LLM 智能体无需修改模型参数即可解决复杂交互任务的有效手段。近期方法通过从执行轨迹中蒸馏可复用经验并基于下游任务反馈演化技能来提升适应性。然而，现有方法主要以自然语言文档表示技能，将过程性逻辑与描述性知识交织在一起，导致技能难以维护和演化。为解决这一局限，我们提出 PASE（程序辅助的可修补技能演化），一个通过将技能与可执行程序关联来迭代演化技能的程序辅助框架。不同于以往主要在自然语言中编码轨迹经验的方法，PASE 将可复用的过程性逻辑分离为可编辑的程序，从而可对可执行组件进行针对性更新，减少反复修改自然语言技能的需求。在多样模型和基准上的大量实验表明，PASE 持续超越所有基线，提升超过 2.8%。进一步分析显示 PASE 具有更强的演化稳定性和泛化能力，凸显程序化知识在技能演化中的关键作用。我们将通过 GitHub 发布所有数据和代码。
translation.brief: 解决技能以自然语言表示导致过程逻辑难以维护演化的问题，核心方法是将可复用过程性逻辑分离为可编辑的程序并与技能关联，实现针对性的可执行组件更新。

papers.title: Software Refactoring Research with Large Language Models: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: Background: Code refactoring is the improvement of code internally without changing the external functionalities of the program. Due to its exhaustive nature, developers often avoid manually refactoring code. Researchers have since looked into utilizing LLMs to automate the task of refactoring. Aim and Method: Despite the promising results, there is a lack of clear un- derstanding of LLMs' effectiveness in automated refactoring. Result: From our literature review we found that: (i) there are various tools that different studies use to enhance and study LLM-driving refactoring, with tools that were used to detect code smells, generate code bases, and compare refactoring outcomes. (ii) Various datasets were collected from multiple open- source projects in multiple programming languages for analysis. These platforms included GitHub, Apache, and F-Droid, with the most popular language collec- ted and analyzed being Java. (iii) One-Shot, Few-Shot, Context-Specific, and Chain-of-Thought prompting methods have been shown to be the most effective depending on the language used. In some instances, being capable of reducing code smell by up to 89%. (iv) The definition of "accuracy" varies significantly across the literature surveyed, as this depends on the context of the study, thus calling for a need to have a standardized measurement for Accuracy. (v) The most often mentioned code smells were Large Class and Long Method, with a lot of studies also not specifying, while the most often applied refactoring type is Extract Method, showing promising results in using LLM to perform this refactoring type. (vi) When working with LLMs, they often generate erroneous code, struggle with more complex refactoring, and often misunderstand the developers' requests and miss refactoring requests.

translation.title: 基于大语言模型的软件重构研究：系统性文献综述
translation.abstract: 背景：代码重构是在不改变程序外部功能的前提下改进代码内部结构，因其繁琐性，开发者常避免手动重构，研究者因此探索利用 LLM 自动化重构。目的与方法：尽管结果令人期待，对 LLM 在自动化重构中有效性的理解仍不清晰。结果：通过文献综述我们发现：(i) 不同研究使用多种工具来增强和研究 LLM 驱动的重构，包括检测代码坏味道、生成代码库和比较重构结果的工具；(ii) 从 GitHub、Apache、F-Droid 等多个开源项目收集了多种编程语言的数据集，其中 Java 是最常被收集和分析的语言；(iii) One-Shot、Few-Shot、上下文特定和思维链等提示方法根据所用语言不同而各有最有效的场景，某些情况下可将代码坏味道减少多达 89%；(iv) 所调研文献中"准确率"的定义差异显著，取决于研究语境，亟需标准化的准确率度量；(v) 最常提及的代码坏味道是 Large Class 和 Long Method，许多研究未明确说明，最常应用的重构类型是 Extract Method，显示出 LLM 执行该重构类型的良好前景；(vi) LLM 常生成错误代码，难以处理更复杂的重构，且常误解开发者请求并遗漏重构需求。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 在自动化代码重构中有效性缺乏清晰认识的问题，通过系统性文献综述梳理相关工具、数据集、提示方法、准确率定义、代码坏味道与重构类型及现存局限。

papers.title: HandsOnAid: Building and Evaluating an Offline First-Aid Assistant for Emergency Response Scenarios
papers.abstract: Emergencies can occur where there is no phone signal and no ambulance nearby. A small language model on a phone can be helpful in such situations, but its advice needs to be safe and accurate. We built HandsOnAid, a 4-bit Gemma 2B model fine-tuned with QLoRA on FirstAidQA dataset, a corpus of 5,550 first-aid question-answer pairs. We compared seven configurations, including the base, 4-bit and 8-bit fine-tuned models, and versions with a length floor, safety gate, or retrieval. We used a 41-pair question-answer bank with medically reviewed references that followed ANZCOR guidelines, and a strict 0-5 score rubric, with twelve safety overrides. Four frontier LLM judges (GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM-5.3) blindly scored every answer, with 45 hidden controls used to check judge reliability. Fine-tuning improved the mean score by +1.08 over the base model to 2.34. The best configuration scored 2.51 out of 5 which was the fine-tuned 4-bit model with retrieval. A medical professional also conducted a blind evaluation of 40 answers across the base, the 4-bit fine-tuned, and the retrieval configurations, and the scores were similar to the LLM judges' average scores. A keyword audit found limited coverage of several details of ANZCOR guidelines in the training corpus, that are required by the rubric, which suggests that missing information in the training data could be a cause of the low scores. On a smartphone device (Pixel 7 Pro) with six CPU threads and no network connection, the 4-bit fine-tuned model produced its first displayable text in 6.86 seconds and a complete answer in 14.88 seconds on average over ten questions.

translation.title: HandsOnAid：为应急响应场景构建并评估离线急救助手
translation.abstract: 紧急情况可能发生在没有手机信号、救护车无法及时到达的地方。手机上的小型语言模型在此类情况下可提供帮助，但其建议必须安全准确。我们构建了 HandsOnAid，一个基于 FirstAidQA 数据集（5550 条急救问答对）用 QLoRA 微调的 4-bit Gemma 2B 模型。我们比较了七种配置，包括基座模型、4-bit 和 8-bit 微调模型，以及带长度下限、安全门控或检索增强的版本。我们使用包含 41 对问答的题库（参考答案经医学审核、遵循 ANZCOR 指南）和严格的 0-5 分评分细则，外加十二条安全覆盖规则。四个前沿 LLM 评判者（GPT-5.6 Sol、Claude Opus 5、DeepSeek V4 Pro、GLM-5.3）盲评所有答案，并使用 45 个隐藏控制项检验评判者可靠性。微调使平均分较基座模型提升 +1.08 至 2.34。最佳配置为带检索的 4-bit 微调模型，得分 2.51/5。一位医学专业人员还对基座、4-bit 微调和检索配置的 40 个答案进行了盲评，评分与 LLM 评判者的平均分相近。关键词审计发现训练语料对评分细则要求的若干 ANZCOR 指南细节覆盖有限，说明训练数据缺失信息可能是低分的原因之一。在无网络连接、六 CPU 线程的智能手机（Pixel 7 Pro）上，4-bit 微调模型在十个问题上平均 6.86 秒输出首个可显示文本，14.88 秒生成完整答案。
translation.brief: 解决无网络信号、救护车无法及时到达场景下急救咨询的问题，核心方法是用 QLoRA 在急救问答数据集上微调小型模型并以多 LLM 评判与人工盲评进行严格评估。

papers.title: Where Do Vision-Language Models Get Left and Right? Position-Code Counterfactuals in Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3
papers.abstract: A vision-language model may take left-right direction from the orientation of image content within patches, its vision transformer's (ViT) position code, or token positions and order in its language model (LLM). Ablations show the ViT code is necessary; we test sufficiency by mirroring only a position code. In Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-4B and InternVL3-2B, mirroring ViT width positions reproduces the flipped-image answer on 84.3-93.2% of CV-Bench left-right questions (Qwen2.5-VL-3B: 87.5%, partly a left fallback). With two options, this also counts disruption; a half-grid shift flips most answers too. With the ViT code intact, LLM-side id and token-order mirrors change few left-right answers in all three series (a weak id test in Qwen2.5-VL). In Qwen2.5-VL-7B the effect sits in the global-attention ViT blocks, mostly the last. On What'sUp, flipping content and token order, not the position code, keeps more on/under than left-right answers at the flipped-image answer. Post hoc analyses qualify these results. On CV-Bench items with located objects, random permutations flip 18.9-31.0 points more answers when reversing the objects' order than when keeping it. On What'sUp, in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL, the share of the left-right changes made by random permutations that land on the mirror relation is mostly below chance. Counted as returns to the original answer, the What'sUp contrast of support with left-right relations is clear only in InternVL3-2B. Most remaining errors give the same relation whichever object is asked about, suggesting that repair may target relation binding, object localization or use of the reference object.

translation.title: 视觉语言模型从哪里获取左右方向信息？Qwen2.5-VL、Qwen3-VL 与 InternVL3 中的位置编码反事实分析
translation.abstract: 视觉语言模型的左右方向判断可能来自图像内容在 patch 中的朝向、其视觉 transformer（ViT）的位置编码，或其语言模型（LLM）中 token 的位置与顺序。消融实验表明 ViT 编码是必要的；我们通过仅镜像位置编码来检验其充分性。在 Qwen2.5-VL-7B、Qwen3-VL-4B 和 InternVL3-2B 中，镜像 ViT 宽度位置可在 84.3-93.2% 的 CV-Bench 左右问题上复现翻转图像的答案（Qwen2.5-VL-3B：87.5%，部分为向左的回退）。在两个选项的情况下，这也构成了干扰；半网格偏移同样能翻转大多数答案。在 ViT 编码完好时，LLM 侧的 id 和 token 顺序镜像在三个系列中都只改变少量左右答案（Qwen2.5-VL 中 id 测试较弱）。在 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 中，该效应位于全局注意力的 ViT 块中，主要在最后几层。在 What'sUp 上，翻转内容和 token 顺序（而非位置编码）时，在翻转图像答案处，on/under 类答案比左右类答案保持得更多。事后分析对这些结果有所限定：在含定位对象的 CV-Bench 项上，随机置换在逆序对象时比保持顺序时多翻转 18.9-31.0 个百分点；在 What'sUp 上，Qwen2.5-VL 和 Qwen3-VL 中随机置换导致的左右变化落在镜像关系上的比例大多低于随机水平。若以回到原始答案计，What'sUp 上左右关系的支持性对比仅在 InternVL3-2B 中明显。多数剩余错误在被询问对象不同时给出相同关系，提示修复可针对关系绑定、对象定位或参考对象的使用。
translation.brief: 研究视觉语言模型左右方向判断的来源问题，核心方法是通过仅镜像 ViT 或 LLM 侧位置编码的反事实干预实验定位方向信息的载体。

papers.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark, Its Reference Defenders, and the Tables Built on Them
papers.abstract: CAGE Challenge 4 is the benchmark on which learned multi-agent cyber defenders are compared. We reproduce its two reference defenders, KEEP and H-MARL Expert, in a pinned container and show that three things read from it measure less than they are taken to measure. First, the simulator silently discards any action asserted for an agent whose previous action is still running, and charges one point for a discarded Restore as for one that runs. The documented observation does not expose the busy flag. Both reference defenders read it in their own wrappers, and switching that check off at evaluation costs KEEP's released policy 99.58 points per episode and H-MARL's 145.98, in both cases the charge for Restores sent to busy agents, with H-MARL's executed actions unchanged step for step. On a supervisory harness, holding interventions until the agent is idle is worth 25.3 and 27.6 points per episode at the published setting. In training, the check decides how a busy step enters the trajectory. Trained without it, KEEP leads at a hundred updates in all four paired seeds and trails from two hundred on in all four. Continued to two thousand updates on three seeds, the repaired recipe ends inside the released interval on one seed and short on two, by 27 and 125 points, a spread across training seeds far wider than the released reproduction interval. Second, the evaluation seeds the environment but not the policy, so a reported mean is one draw, and 88.9% of per-episode outcome variance is the policy's own sampling draw. Third, recovery precision depends on the truth it is scored against. Across five published comparison tables, none states the artifact, sampling, criterion and adversary that would make its numbers comparable. We release the instrument, our patches to both defenders, the traces and checkpoints behind every number, and a five-item disclosure checklist.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Task Offloading in Mobile Edge Computing-Empowered Space-Air-Ground Integrated Internet-of-Things Networks
papers.abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC)-empowered spaceair-ground integrated Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks (SAGIINs) provide a promising solution for computation-intensive tasks generated by mobile IoT devices (IDs). However, task offloading in SAGIINs is challenging due to time-varying IDto-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) channels, intermittent LEO satellite service availability, and the coupling among UAV trajectory, communication, computation, and energy decisions. This paper investigates an energy-efficient task offloading and UAV trajectory planning problem in an MEC-empowered SAGIIN, where one UAV acts as both an aerial relay and an MEC server, and multiple LEO satellites provide supplementary computing resources. The UAV trajectory planning, task splitting, and computing resource allocation are jointly optimized to minimize the total system energy consumption under task completion, communication, computation, flight region, and satellite service window constraints. The resulting non-convex problem is decomposed into a UAV trajectory planning subproblem and a task splitting and computing resource allocation subproblem. To solve the former, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-assisted large language model (LLM)-enhanced deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, termed RLD, is proposed. The latter is shown to be convex and can be solved by using CVXPY for a given UAV trajectory. A weighted retrieval score is further designed to balance ID mobility-pattern similarity and historical UAV trajectory energy performance. Simulation results show that RLD completes all computational tasks in previously unseen test scenarios while consuming less total energy than the benchmark algorithms.

papers.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
papers.abstract: Formal verification using proof assistants provides strong correctness guarantees for software, but constructing proofs remains labor-intensive and requires significant expertise. Recent approaches based on large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in automating proof synthesis. However, these approaches typically constrain the model to a rigid tactic-generation loop, in which the surrounding system controls premise retrieval, proof-state management, and backtracking. We introduce ProofCoder, an agentic proof-synthesis system for Rocq that approaches theorem proving from a coding-agent perspective. Rather than generating tactics within a fixed loop, ProofCoder reasons continuously throughout proof search and uses proof-assistant feedback to decide when to gather additional information, inspect proof states, revise previously generated proof fragments, or backtrack to an earlier point in the proof. This allows it to iteratively construct, repair, and refine proofs, at either tactic-level or whole-proof granularity. We evaluate ProofCoder on 280 challenging verification tasks from the AutoRocq Benchmark. On the best-performing configurations, ProofCoder increases proof success from 47% to 60% over the state-of-theart AutoRocq system, corresponding to a 27.7% relative improvement at approximately half the cost. Our ablations identify continuous reasoning as a key design choice: without it, the agent solves fewer lemmas at substantially higher cost, backtracks four to six times more often, and more frequently discards its own revisions. Whole-proof and tactic-level generation achieve similar success rates but follow distinct search and repair strategies. These results suggest that effective automated software verification requires more than improved tactic selection: continuous reasoning and feedback-guided proof revision are critical ingredients for robust proof synthesis.

papers.title: Looking One Step Ahead: An Anticipation-guided Agent for Object State Readout in Videos
papers.abstract: Understanding the progress of an activity requires tracking how the objects involved change over time. Object state readout provides this information by describing a target object's states and transitions across video frames. Although multimodal large language models (MLLMs) generate detailed visual descriptions, these descriptions may leave the attributes needed to distinguish successive states insufficiently specified. In this paper, we propose look-ahead state readout (LASER), an anticipation-guided agent for object state readout that uses possible next-step changes to determine which attributes to inspect in the present. Given temporally ordered frames and a target object, LASER converts anticipated changes into targeted visual questions and inspects the current frame to establish attribute values. It then checks state readouts and forecasts against independent observations of subsequent frames, refining a state record used to generate the final description. Reusable textual observation skills guide this process and are refined by tracing discrepancies with reference captions to the responsible instructions. Candidate revisions are selected on separate videos based on improved caption quality without increased contradictions with reference facts. Model parameters remain frozen throughout adaptation and inference, and the revised skills remain fixed during evaluation. Experiment results and further analysis on OSCaR and PLM RCap show consistent improvements of LASER over strong baselines and existing approaches, which demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve expert-level diagnostic accuracy in static evaluations, where the model receives a curated vignette or case report that already condenses the diagnostically relevant findings. Such evaluations measure inference over already selected evidence; the evaluations do not account for the inquiry used to obtain it. In clinical practice, however, diagnosis is an iterative process of inquiry. Clinicians take the patient's history, or anamnesis (Hx), through targeted questioning, examine the patient, and request and interpret tests, progressively narrowing the differential until they reach a final diagnosis (Dx). We introduce Hx2Dx ARENA, an interactive benchmark of 1'000 clinical cases from the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM). Each case is a simulated encounter that proceeds from initial presentation through history taking and physical examination to diagnostic workup. We evaluate open- and closed-source LLMs under multiple configurations. Performance varies considerably across models in the interactive setting, and every model loses diagnostic accuracy relative to the static setting, where the full case is presented upfront. The ability to ask the right questions accounts for much of both the gap between models and the loss of accuracy: diagnosis improves as questions become more targeted and build a more complete clinical picture. LLMs thus reason well once the relevant data are available but remain limited in hypothesis-driven information gathering, in knowing what to ask in order to know. Closing this gap is a prerequisite for their safe integration into real-world diagnostic workflows.
